frequency_question: How often do partisan electoral integrity or voting bills passed by one chamber successfully clear the second chamber and reach enactment within a single congress?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone federal voting or election administration bills passed by the House (or Senate) that propose sweeping changes to voter registration or voting rules. Excludes routine bipartisan omnibus appropriations riders and technical electoral count reform acts.

cases.name: Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act

coverage_note: 4 named episodes representing major single-chamber-passed federal electoral reform pushes since 2000.
known_gaps: Excludes minor committee-level markers that never received a floor vote in the originating chamber.
skeleton: Four distinct major partisan or sweeping federal election reform initiatives advanced by a single chamber during divided or narrow-margin control eras over the past 26 years.
validity_reason: Valid until the conclusion of the current electoral and congressional alignment cycle.
